describes: app-import.js §16 — the progressive load / import engine
contract: The import engine is the app's only inbound path, and what it produces is a SEQUENCE, not a value: reset, prepare, then per train append -> warm -> draw -> list -> progress, then one authoritative render, then finish. A port that lands on the same store having reported progress in a different order is a port whose progressive load looks wrong on screen and whose partial states cannot be reasoned about. The per-train step is the composition of BOTH front doors — normalizeImportedTrain, then makeUniqueTrainId, then validateTrain on the exported shape — and that composition accepts things neither door accepts alone.

cases.label: a stop whose name is a number
cases.note: stopName returns the raw value as a truthiness test, and canonicalStopShape then spells it with String() — so the validator only ever sees "12".

cases.label: ride_segment is the string "false"
cases.note: a non-empty string is truthy, so this RIDES the segment it says it does not.

cases.label: route_sections is the number 0
cases.note: validateTrain skips a falsy-but-present route_sections entirely; the import path does not skip it, it REPLACES it with [] — so the two doors disagree about what the train even contains.

cases.note: same falsy-skip in the validator, same replacement with the canonical defaults on import.

cases.label: a four-digit station code that is a number
cases.note: rejected — but on its LENGTH, not its type: the grammar wants six digits, and 3770 spells four of them.
cases.error: Train 1 stop 1: n02_station_code must be a six-digit N02_005c, a TDX StationUID, or null.

cases.label: a six-digit station code that is a number
cases.note: ACCEPTED: stationCodeSystem coerces with String() before matching, so a JSON number is a valid N02_005c. The import path keeps it a number all the way into the canonical store — which is the one place the Swift model cannot follow, because Stop.n02StationCode is a String?.

cases.note: jsonspec §8.6.4 notwithstanding, nothing checks it: this validates, exports, and draws nothing.

cases.label: direction is a number
cases.note: accepted by both doors — and normalizeImportedTrain keeps the NUMBER, because `train.direction || "down"` never coerces.

cases.label: visible is the string "yes"
cases.note: the test is `!== false`, so every value except false means visible.

cases.label: visible is 0
train_type is a number
cases.note: THE asymmetry: validateTrain rejects a numeric train_type outright, but normalizeImportedTrain has already coerced it to "" by the time the validator runs — so the import engine ACCEPTS what the validator refuses.

cases.label: an id that is not in the documented charset
cases.note: REJECTED, though normalizeImportedTrain never applies TRAIN_ID_PATTERN: the pattern arrives with the second door.
cases.error: Train 1: id must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ (letters, digits, "_" and "-").

cases.label: an id with surrounding whitespace
cases.note: ACCEPTED and silently trimmed. makeUniqueTrainId runs between the two doors and trims the base, so the id validateTrain sees is not the id the document contained.

cases.label: an id that is only whitespace
cases.note: ACCEPTED as the id "train": a whitespace-only base is falsy after trimming, and makeUniqueTrainId's second fallback catches it.

cases.label: a stop whose name is null
cases.note: the import whitelist's guard is `"name" in stop`, so this passes door one and is caught by door two.
cases.error: Train 1 stop 1: name is required.

cases.label: a stop row that is null
cases.note: one of the three inputs that CRASH validateTrain with a TypeError — but not through this door: normalizeImportedStop rejects it as a plain Error first, so the crash is unreachable from an import.

seedCases.note: the test is `=== true`, so a truthy non-boolean falls through to the features branch.

seedCases.label: a cache_key that is a number
seedCases.note: `typeof !== "string"` rejects it before the features are looked at.

sampleNameCases.label: a day the manifest does not have
sampleNameCases.note: falls back to the WHOLE sample rather than loading nothing — but the mode still says sample-single, because the mode is decided by the argument and the names by the manifest.

sampleNameCases.note: an empty array IS an array, so this loads zero parts — sampleManifestDates would never have offered this day, but an explicit request reaches it.
